headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can emit content and has broad network egress; Agent B reads files and processes documents, so A’s outputs could be copied into B’s inputs through a shared workspace or manual bridge. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high, but the interaction is plausible and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF A-generated content is placed into a file that B ingests as a document, injection becomes active.
IF the two agents share a workspace or clipboard, B may parse attacker-controlled instructions from A's output.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs by B.
Add a human review step before B processes any A-produced text.
Use provenance labels on files passed between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering at the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write files and touches documents/images/text, while A has broad network egress. If sensitive documents are present in a shared workspace, B can process them and A can potentially exfiltrate derived content through its network access. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so I rate medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory containing sensitive documents, leakage becomes plausible.
IF A receives B-produced summaries or extracted text, A can transmit them off-host via network egress.
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside any shared path.
Restrict A to non-sensitive inputs only.
Turn off B processing for confidential folders.
Review outbound destinations for A before use.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and supports_multiple_instances, while A’s profile does not show write access. There is no direct write-write conflict, but B can still contend with other writers if the orchestrator places both on the same mutable workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF A and B are assigned the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF B runs multiple instances against one workspace, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize B jobs per workspace.
Use file locks for shared outputs.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same documents.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B processes documents and can write outputs, so if A’s generated content is fed into B without verification, B may propagate errors or fabricated claims into downstream artifacts. A does not have documented action-taking authority, so this is not high, but the A-to-B handoff is a realistic default workflow risk.
conditions: IF B consumes A-produced text as authoritative input, errors can cascade into B outputs.
IF B’s outputs are used downstream without review, incorrect extracted facts may be propagated.
mitigations: Require source citations before B accepts A output.
Add a verification pass on B outputs.
Flag low-confidence extractions for review.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly calls external APIs and has privacy-policy/docs URLs, while A has broad network egress but no data classes touched. There is no evidence of regulated data or residency mismatch, so compliance exposure is limited to policy/process gaps rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B’s external API calls, policy review is required.
IF A is used to transmit content subject to retention rules, logging controls matter.
mitigations: Review vendor privacy terms.
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention settings for B.
Limit A outbound destinations.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
